reportSubtitle: Restructured Campaign Week 1, Best CPL Ever, Lookalike Video Outlier
summary:
First week running the restructured 4 ad set campaign and it produced our best week to date: 7 demos at $43.92 CPL on $307 spend. That beats last week (5 demos at $55.36) on every dimension, and beats every prior week of the campaign too.

The story inside the breakdown is the Lookalike Video ad set. 4 of the 7 demos came from it at a $16.54 CPL, roughly a third of any prior week's cost per lead. The other three active ad sets each delivered 1 demo at $68 to $87 CPL. With only one week of post-restructure data, I want to be careful not to overweight one strong week from a single ad set on a small sample.

On the self-serve side, paid-tier signup intent moved up. 9 of 20 plan signup clicks this week were on Pro or Creator (45% paid share, up from 33% on the prior 30-day snapshot). Pro alone hit 5 clicks in 7 days, more than half its prior 30-day total.

No budget changes this week. Next Friday we'll have 2 weeks of post-restructure data on each ad set and can make a more confident reallocation call rather than reacting to one week of small-sample variance.

metrics.label: Ad Spend
metrics.note: Up from $276.81 last week. AU/DE/FR ad set retired as planned.

metrics.label: Leads (Demo Bookings)
metrics.note: Best week of the campaign. Lookalike Video drove 4 of 7.

metrics.label: Cost per Lead
metrics.note: Down from $55.36 last week. New all-time low.

metrics.label: Paid-Tier Signup Clicks
metrics.note: 5 Pro + 4 Creator. 45% of plan signup clicks landed on a paid tier (up from 33% prior 30 days).

tierBreakdown.adSpendComparison: $1,317/mo equivalent ad spend, breakeven would require ~3 months retention per paid-tier user

charts.title: Plan Signup Clicks by Tier (7-Day)
charts.note: 55% of self-serve interest is on the free tier this week, down from 67% on prior 30-day snapshot. Pro tier clicks alone (5) are more than half its prior 30-day total (9).

findings.title: Lookalike Video Drove 4 of 7 Demos at $16.54 CPL
findings.description: Best single ad set performance of the campaign. The other three active ad sets each produced 1 demo at $68 to $87 CPL on roughly equal $66 to $87 spend. Lookalike Static at $67.97 CPL is meaningfully behind its video counterpart even though both target the same audience, suggesting creative format is doing real work here, not just audience selection.

findings.title: Paid-Tier Signup Mix Shifted Up
findings.description: Pro hit 5 clicks in 7 days versus 9 clicks across the entire prior 30 days. Creator stayed steady at 4. Basic dropped from 67% to 55% share of plan signup clicks. Total click volume held flat at 20, but the tier mix moved toward higher revenue intent.

findings.title: Modal Opens Up Despite Tighter Targeting
findings.description: cal_modal_opened jumped to 20 (from 12 last week) on 164 unique visitors. That's a 12.2% modal-open rate, up from 4.0% last week. Narrowing the audience age to 32-48 and retiring secondary geos appears to have concentrated higher-intent visitors rather than thinned out demand.

actions.title: Ran Restructured Campaign for One Full Week, No Mid-Week Adjustments
actions.description: Held all 4 ad sets at $12.50/day each as launched on Apr 10. No budget shifts, no creative swaps, no audience tweaks. Goal was to get a clean week of post-restructure data before making any reallocation decisions.

nextSteps: Hold all ad set budgets at $12.50/day for one more week to get 2 weeks of post-restructure data before any reallocation
Watch whether Lookalike Video sustains its $16-20 CPL range or regresses with more volume
Compare Lookalike Static vs Lookalike Video creative performance once both have a larger sample to determine whether to retire static or refresh the creative
